title: Truing a Refined Fuels Contracted Price Against What the Member Was Last Billed
content:
The contracted price carried on an account under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts is trued against the price the member has actually been billed on its will-call stops. Whether such a stop was billed in the recent quarter, and how the adjusted price stands against it, decide where the price of record lands.

**What a will-call stop is.** A will-call stop is one the records show the member called in, and not one run to the automatic keep-full schedule, run as an emergency, run after hours or made to fill against a booking.

**Where 1 or more will-call stops were billed on the account in the three months ending on the handling date and the adjusted price stands above the posted price of record**, the truing rule puts the contracted price of record at the posted price of record.

**Where 1 or more such stops were billed in that window and the adjusted price stands at or under the posted price of record**, the truing rule puts the contracted price of record at the mean of the adjusted price and the posted price of record, carried to four decimal places.

**Where no such stop was billed in that window**, the truing rule leaves the contracted price of record at the adjusted price.

**The posted price of record** for this purpose is the price billed on the most recent will-call stop, carried to four decimal places.

| Will-call stops billed in the three months ending on the handling date | The adjusted price against the posted price of record | Where the contracted price of record lands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 or more | Above it | At the posted price of record |
| 1 or more | At it, or under it | At the mean of the two, to four decimal places |
| None | Either way | At the adjusted price |

*Hypothetical.* An account with a will-call stop billed two months ago, whose most recent will-call stop was billed at 2.0000 USD per gallon, and whose adjusted price comes out at 2.2000, takes the posted price of record: 2.0000 USD per gallon. Had the adjusted price come out at 1.8000, the two would be averaged and the price of record would be 1.9000 USD per gallon. Had the adjusted price stood at 2.0000 exactly, it would stand at or under the posted price of record, the two would be averaged, and the price of record would again be 2.0000. With no will-call stop billed in the quarter, the adjusted price would stand as it was.
